title: Suspension of the Schedule Guarantee for Arrears on a Retrofit Project
content:
# Suspension of the Schedule Guarantee for Arrears

Time a project under Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects lost because the owner's account fell behind does not run against the company's guarantee.

## Rule

Where a remobilisation fee stands billed on the project, work having been stopped for non-payment and restarted, the guarantee is suspended for the number of days past due at which the project's class stops work.

Where no remobilisation fee stands billed on the project but a late fee has been raised on it, the guarantee is suspended for half that number of days, that is for 50 per cent of it, rounded to a whole day.

Where no remobilisation fee and no late fee stand on the project, the guarantee is not suspended, and 0 days are taken out of the count.

## Judgement table

| Remobilisation fee billed on the project | Late fee raised on the project | Days the guarantee is suspended for |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | the number of days past due at which the class stops work |
| yes | no | the number of days past due at which the class stops work |
| no | yes | half that number, rounded to a whole day |
| no | no | none |

A remobilisation fee governs wherever it stands billed: a project that was stopped and restarted lost the whole of the stoppage period, whatever late fees also sit on it.

## Worked days (hypothetical, class stopping work after 21 days past due)

A project carrying a remobilisation fee has its guarantee suspended for 21 days. A project carrying no remobilisation fee but one late fee has it suspended for 11 days, half of 21 rounded to a whole day. A project carrying neither has no suspension at all.
